# Issue Tracker CLI Guide

The `flu git issue` command provides a full-featured CLI interface to the Forgejo issue tracker, allowing you to manage issues without leaving the terminal. This command is part of the unified git workflow management system, powered by **fh-commons**.

## Quick Reference

> **Issue Backend:** All `flu issue` commands accept `--backend BACKEND`
> (`forgejo` | `psql`; default: `forgejo`). Projects using the psql backend
> (e.g. PAT) should pass `--backend psql` or set `issue.backend_default`
> in `.fhc-config.json`. Note: `bulk`, `move`, and `report` subcommands
> do not yet support psql (see #2520).

```bash
# List issues
flu git issue list                    # Open issues only (default)
flu git issue list --all              # All issues (open and closed)
flu git issue list --state closed     # Closed issues only

# View issue details
flu git issue view 5                  # View issue #5 with all comments

# Create issues
flu git issue create                  # Interactive mode (prompts for input)
flu git issue create --title "Title"  # With title only
flu git issue create --title "Title" --body "Description"  # With title and body
flu git issue create --title "Title" --body-file /tmp/description.md  # From file
flu cat /tmp/description.md | flu git issue create --title "Title" --body-file -

# Comment on issues
flu git issue comment 5               # Interactive mode
flu git issue comment 5 "Your comment text"  # Direct comment
flu git issue comment 5 --body-file /tmp/comment.md
flu cat /tmp/comment.md | flu git issue comment 5 --body-file -

# Close and reopen
flu git issue close 5                 # Close issue #5
flu git issue reopen 5                # Reopen issue #5

# Search issues
flu git issue search "keyword"        # Search in titles and descriptions

# Label management
flu git issue label 5 bug priority:high    # Add labels to issue
flu git issue unlabel 5 bug                # Remove labels from issue
flu git issue labels                       # List available labels
```

## Features

### Read Operations (No Authentication Required)
- List issues (`list`)
- View issue details (`view`)
- Search issues (`search`)

These commands work immediately without any setup.

### Write Operations (Authentication Required)
- Create issues (`create`)
- Add comments (`comment`)
- Close issues (`close`)
- Reopen issues (`reopen`)

These commands require a Forgejo access token.

## Authentication Setup

### Option 1: Project Directory (Recommended)
Store your token in the project root:

```bash
echo 'YOUR_TOKEN' > .forgejo_token
```

This keeps the token with your project and is automatically ignored by git.

### Option 2: Environment Variable
Set the token as an environment variable:

```bash
export FORGEJO_TOKEN='your_token_here'
```

Add to your `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc` to make it permanent.

### Option 3: User Config Directory
Store the token in your home directory:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/forgejo
echo 'YOUR_TOKEN' > ~/.config/forgejo/token
chmod 600 ~/.config/forgejo/token
```

### Getting a Token

1. Go to https://git.jdp21.com/user/settings/applications
2. Under "Generate New Token", enter a name (e.g., "CLI token")
3. Click "Generate Token"
4. Copy the token immediately (it won't be shown again)
5. Save it using one of the methods above

## Integration with Web UI

The CLI and web UI share the same backend, so:
- Issues created via CLI appear instantly in the web UI
- Comments and changes sync in real-time
- Both interfaces work with the same issue numbers

**Web UI:** https://git.jdp21.com/jpierce/fluxaos/issues

## Enhanced PR Features

In addition to issue management, the `flu git` command includes PR features:

```bash
# Checkout a PR branch locally
flu git pr-checkout 52           # Checkout PR #52

# Review a PR interactively
flu git pr-review 52             # Interactive review workflow

# Approve a PR
flu git pr-approve 52            # Approve PR #52

# Request changes on a PR
flu git pr-reject 52             # Request changes on PR #52

# Clean up merged PR branches
flu pr clean                     # Delete all merged PR branches
```

Only the PR checkout/review/approve/reject commands require the
[tea CLI](https://gitea.com/gitea/tea) to be installed and configured.

## Usage Examples

### Creating an Issue Workflow

```bash
# Create a bug report
flu git issue create -t "Bug: Video converter fails on MKV files" \
  -b "When converting MKV files, the converter crashes with error..."

# Create a long-form issue from file (preserves markdown)
flu git issue create --title "Bug: Empty folders not cleaned" --body-file /tmp/issue-description.md

# Use stdin when title is already set
cat /tmp/issue-description.md | flu git issue create --title "Bug: Empty folders not cleaned" --body-file -

# Or use interactive mode for longer descriptions
flu git issue create
```

### Tracking Work Progress

```bash
# List open issues to see what needs work
flu git issue list

# Work on issue #5
flu git issue view 5

# Add progress updates
flu git issue comment 5 "Started work on this issue"
flu git issue comment 5 "Fixed the root cause in commit abc123"

# Close when done
flu git issue close 5
```

### Searching and Investigation

```bash
# Find all issues related to backup
flu git issue search "backup"

# Find all issues about video processing
flu git issue search "video"

# View details of found issues
flu git issue view 12
```

### Review Workflow

```bash
# See all open issues
flu git issue list

# Check closed issues
flu git issue list --state closed

# Reopen if needed
flu git issue reopen 8
```

## Git Integration

Reference issues in commit messages:
```bash
git commit -m "Fix video conversion for MKV files

Resolves #5"
```

Forgejo will automatically:
- Link the commit to issue #5
- Close the issue when merged to main (with "closes #5" or "fixes #5")

## LLM Integration

The CLI is designed to work with LLMs (like Claude):
- LLMs can create issues programmatically
- Add comments with progress updates
- Close issues when work is complete
- Search for related issues

Example LLM workflow:
```bash
# LLM discovers a bug while working
flu git issue create -t "Bug: Empty folders not cleaned" \
  -b "Found during cleanup task. The empty_folder script..."

# Standard long-form pattern for LLM/non-interactive flows:
# - use --body-file /path/to/text.md for file input
# - use --body-file - when stdin is already prepared
# Keep --body for short inline fields.

# LLM adds investigation notes
flu git issue comment 7 "Root cause: recursive check fails on symlinks"

# LLM commits fix and closes issue
git commit -m "Fix empty folder detection for symlinks (closes #7)"
flu git issue close 7
```

## Tips and Best Practices

### Creating Good Issues
- Use clear, descriptive titles
- Include steps to reproduce for bugs
- Add relevant context (error messages, file paths)
- Tag related issues in the description (#5, #12)

### Using Comments Effectively
- Add progress updates
- Reference commits with fixes
- Ask questions and request clarification
- Document decisions and reasoning

### Organizing with Search
- Use consistent keywords in titles
- Search before creating duplicates
- Use issue numbers to reference related issues

### Integration with CLI Workflow
```bash
# Morning routine: Check open issues
flu git issue list

# Work on high priority items
flu git issue view 3
flu git issue comment 3 "Starting work on this"

# During development
git commit -m "Implement feature (part of #3)"

# When complete
flu git issue comment 3 "Completed - deployed to production"
flu git issue close 3
```

## Authentication Priority

The CLI checks for tokens in this order:
1. Token file path specified in `config/common.json` (default: `.forgejo_token`)
2. `FORGEJO_TOKEN` environment variable
3. `~/.config/forgejo/token` file

First token found is used.

## Configuration

Forgejo settings are stored in `config/common.json` under the `forgejo` key:

```json
"forgejo": {
    "base_url": "https://git.jdp21.com",
    "api_url": "https://git.jdp21.com/api/v1",
    "owner": "jpierce",
    "repo": "fluxaos",
    "token_file": ".forgejo_token"
}
```

This allows you to customize the Forgejo instance URL, repository, and token location.

## Managing Labels

Labels help categorize and organize issues. The default labels include: `bug`, `enhancement`, `question`, `documentation`, `duplicate`, `help wanted`, `invalid`, and `wontfix`.

### Creating/Managing Labels

**Direct URL (recommended):**
```
https://git.jdp21.com/jpierce/fluxaos/labels
```

**Note:** The Labels management page is not always visible in the Settings navigation. Using the direct URL above is the easiest way to access it.

### Using Labels on Issues

**Web UI:**
- When viewing an issue, click the gear icon next to "Labels" in the right sidebar
- Select one or more labels from the dropdown
- Labels are applied immediately

**CLI:**
Labels are displayed when viewing or listing issues, and can be used for organization and filtering.

## Error Handling

### "Authentication required"
- You need a token for write operations
- See [Authentication Setup](#authentication-setup)

### "Issue not found"
- Check the issue number
- Use `flu git issue list --all` to see all issues

### "Connection failed"
- Verify Forgejo server is running
- Check network connectivity to git.jdp21.com
